course.title: Office and Administrative Assistant English
course.summary: Coordinate calendars, handle calls, support meetings, manage document versions, query supplies, welcome visitors, arrange travel, and hand over competing tasks clearly.
course.roles: Office assistants, administrative assistants, reception administrators, and team support staff
course.scope_note: All organizations, appointments, documents, prices, policies, and incidents are fictional English practice. This is not legal, financial, immigration, security, or records-retention advice. Follow the employer's actual purchasing, access, privacy, travel, and approval arrangements. Sample policies and delegated responsibilities apply only to the stated exercise.

sources.title: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants
O*NET OnLine: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive

modules.title: Scheduling across calendars and time zones
collocations: place a tentative hold: reserve a proposed time without calling it confirmed
check for a conflict: identify appointments that overlap
allow a buffer: leave time between scheduled commitments
confirm the time zone: state which local clock time an invitation uses

case.brief: A colleague asks for a 3:00 meeting with another office. For this fictional date, 3:00 in the colleague's office equals noon at the other office. The request does not identify whose time is intended. Both calendars are open at that equivalent time; confirm the intended time before sending invitations.
case.model: When you say three o'clock, do you mean three in your office's time zone? On this date, that would be noon for the other office. Both calendars are open then, but I haven't sent an invitation. Please confirm the intended local time so I can label the meeting accurately.

workshop.title: Resolve the time reference before booking
workshop.goal: Confirm whose clock a proposed meeting time refers to.
workshop.explanation: A calendar opening is not acceptance. State both local times for the supplied date and distinguish a hold from a confirmed meeting.
frames: Do you mean ___ in ___ time?
On that date, it will be ___ for ___.
I've placed a hold; ___ is still unconfirmed.
workshop.after: Do you mean three here, which is noon for the other office on that date?
workshop.reason: The question identifies the missing time reference.

questions.prompt:
Colleague: I mean three in our office, which is noon there on this date.
Assistant: I'll show ____ on the invitation.
feedback: Correct. Both local times make the intended shared moment clear.
That would describe different moments under the supplied time difference.
That also changes the intended local time for this office.
An unspecified time would leave the original ambiguity unresolved.

questions.prompt:
Colleague: You reserved the time, but Morgan hasn't replied. Is the meeting confirmed?
Assistant: No, the calendar entry is ____.
feedback: Correct. The time is reserved temporarily while acceptance remains outstanding.
Morgan has not replied, so acceptance cannot be recorded.
A reserved opening does not by itself confirm the meeting.
No reply does not establish that Morgan has declined.

workshop.role_b: Colleague: mean three in your own office; can explain the supplied noon equivalent when asked.
workshop.challenge: One participant calls the time lunchtime. Check their local time rather than treating the phrase as a new booking request.

modules.title: Taking useful calls and passing accurate messages
collocations: take a message: record the caller's relevant details
read the number back: repeat a phone number to check accuracy
put a caller through: connect them to the intended recipient
confirm the purpose of the call: ask what the caller needs without requesting unnecessary private details

case.brief: Caller Lena Park needs the facilities team about delivery D18, not the finance team about an invoice. Facilities extension is 214. Lena requests a callback before 4:00, but availability is unknown. Ask for the delivery reference and preferred contact route, then relay the requested deadline without promising it.
case.model: Could I confirm that your call concerns delivery D18 for facilities, rather than an invoice query for finance? I'll route the message to extension 214. Please confirm your preferred callback details. I'll include your request for a response before four, but I haven't confirmed the team's availability.

workshop.title: Collect the details needed for the right recipient
workshop.goal: Request purpose, reference, and contact information without promising a callback time.
workshop.explanation: A caller's requested deadline is not a colleague's commitment. Read back ambiguous names or numbers and keep the message focused.
frames: Is this about ___ or ___?
Let me read that reference back: ___.
You've requested a callback by ___; I'll pass that on.
workshop.after: I'll pass on your request for a callback before four; the team hasn't confirmed that time.
workshop.reason: The caller's preference remains distinct from a promise.

questions.prompt:
Caller: This is about the delivery, not its invoice.
Assistant: I'll route your message to ____.
feedback: Correct. Facilities is responsible for delivery D18 in this case.
The caller explicitly excluded an invoice query.
A payments queue would misroute the stated delivery concern.
Invoice approval is not the subject of this call.

questions.prompt:
Caller: Can they call before four?
Assistant: I'll pass on your ____ for that time.
feedback: Correct. The time is requested but not confirmed.
No commitment to that time has been received.
The return call has not yet happened.
No appointment has been accepted by the recipient.

workshop.role_b: Caller: Lena Park, reference D18, want facilities and a reply before four; can give a work callback number orally.
workshop.challenge: The caller says they already spoke to accounts. Confirm whether the current question is still about physical delivery.

modules.title: Preparing meetings and confirming action points
collocations: circulate the agenda: share the planned meeting topics with attendees
confirm the action owner: identify who has agreed to carry out a task
capture the decision: record what the meeting actually agreed
defer an item: move a topic to a later discussion

case.brief: A meeting has ten minutes left and two agenda items: printer replacement and visitor signage. The chair prioritizes the printer decision. Sam can obtain two quotes by Thursday; nobody has approved a purchase. Ask the group to confirm that action and defer signage to the next meeting.
case.model: We have ten minutes left, and the chair has prioritized the printer item. Sam, can you confirm you'll obtain two quotes by Thursday? I'll record that as the action, not as purchase approval. Can we move visitor signage to the next agenda and confirm whether anyone needs that discussed sooner?

workshop.title: Close a discussion with a specific action
workshop.goal: Help participants confirm a task, owner, and deadline.
workshop.explanation: Distinguish discussion, action, and decision. Obtaining quotes is not the same as approving an order.
frames: Who will take ___, and by when?
The agreed action is ___; no decision on ___ yet.
Can we defer ___ until ___?
workshop.before: Sam will sort out the printer.
workshop.after: Sam will obtain two quotes by Thursday; no purchase is approved.
workshop.reason: The record states a checkable task and avoids inventing a decision.

questions.prompt:
Chair: We only agreed to obtain prices.
Assistant: The minutes should record ____.
feedback: Correct. This preserves the quote task and the unresolved purchase decision.
No purchase approval was given in the meeting.
No supplier appointment was described or completed.
No replacement equipment has been delivered.

questions.prompt:
Chair: Sam may send the quotes early, but Thursday is the deadline.
Assistant: Sam will obtain two quotes ____ Thursday.
feedback: Correct. 'By Thursday' means no later than Thursday and permits earlier delivery.
'Until' describes a continuing action up to a time, not this completion deadline.
'Since' normally marks a starting point continuing into a later period.
'From' identifies a starting point, not the latest completion date.

workshop.role_b: Chair: prioritize the printer; confirm Sam can obtain two quotes by Thursday; signage can wait unless someone raises a concrete urgency.
workshop.challenge: An attendee says the minutes should list a printer purchase. Clarify the actual decision before ending.

modules.title: Checking document versions and access
collocations: confirm the current version: identify which revision should be used
check the attachment: verify which file was actually sent
request viewing access: ask for permission to read without implying editing rights
replace an outdated link: provide a link to the intended current document

case.brief: An assistant sent version 2 of a visitor guide, but version 3 was approved this morning. The older version has the wrong reception floor. The current guide is in the shared folder; one recipient lacks viewing access. Correct the message and request access from the document owner without widening permissions independently.
case.model: I sent version two, which gives the wrong reception floor. I'm sorry for the confusion. Version three was approved this morning and is the current guide in the shared folder. I'll send its link and ask the document owner to resolve your viewing access before you rely on the guide.

workshop.title: Correct the file and the recipient's usable access
workshop.goal: Repair a version error without assuming a link works for everyone.
workshop.explanation: State the current revision and the consequential difference. A correct link is not useful until the intended recipient can open it.
frames: I sent version ___; the current version is ___.
The corrected detail is ___.
Can you confirm you can view ___?
workshop.before: The file is somewhere in the folder.
workshop.after: Version three is current; I'll send its link and check your viewing access.
workshop.reason: The recipient knows which file to use and what remains unresolved.

questions.prompt:
Recipient: I have the link, but it says access denied.
Assistant: The unresolved issue is your ____.
feedback: Correct. Access denied indicates the recipient lacks the required permission.
The revision is current; it does not resolve denied viewing access.
No unsupported format message was reported in this case.
The reported problem concerns permission rather than attachment size.

questions.prompt:
Recipient: Which guide should I use now?
Assistant: Use ____ once your viewing access is confirmed.
feedback: Correct. Version three is the current approved guide in this case.
Version two contains the incorrect reception-floor detail.
Download order does not establish the approved current revision.
The oldest saved copy may contain superseded information.

workshop.role_b: Recipient: have version two and a denied-access message on the new link; need the correct reception floor.
workshop.challenge: The recipient asks you to make the whole folder public. Request the necessary limited access from its owner instead.

modules.title: Querying office supplies and delivery differences
collocations: match the delivery to the order: compare received items with the stated request
report a short delivery: notify the supplier that fewer items arrived than expected
ask for a revised delivery date: request an updated arrival estimate
confirm the outstanding quantity: state how many ordered items remain undelivered

case.brief: Purchase order P44 is for twelve archive boxes. The delivery note lists twelve, but the checked shipment contains ten. No second package or backorder is documented. Ask the supplier to confirm the outstanding two and whether another shipment is planned; do not approve payment or claim theft.
case.model: Purchase order P44 lists twelve archive boxes, and the delivery note also lists twelve. We received ten in the checked shipment, leaving a difference of two. Could you confirm whether another package is due or whether this is a short delivery, and give us the next update time?

workshop.title: Ask a supplier about a specific mismatch
workshop.goal: Give order, stated quantity, received quantity, and the response needed.
workshop.explanation: A document saying delivered does not establish the physical count. Ask about the two missing units without inventing their cause or arrival date.
frames: The order lists ___; we received ___.
Could you confirm whether ___?
Please give us the next update by ___ if agreed.
workshop.after: P44 lists twelve boxes, but the checked shipment contains ten; are two still due?
workshop.reason: The supplier receives an identifiable discrepancy and a focused question.

questions.prompt:
Colleague: Ten of twelve boxes arrived, but there's no notice about the other two. Are they confirmed as a backorder?
Assistant: ____.
options: We've reported a short delivery; a backorder hasn't been confirmed
We've received confirmation that both are on backorder
The delivery note confirms that another shipment is due
The physical count confirms that all twelve have arrived
feedback: Correct. The reported shortage is known; the supplier's status for the remaining two is not.
No backorder confirmation has been supplied in this case.
The note lists twelve but does not identify another shipment.
The physical count is ten, so it cannot confirm receipt of twelve.

questions.prompt:
Colleague: I submitted a requisition. Has that automatically placed the supplier order?
Assistant: No, it is still an ____.
feedback: Correct. A requisition requests goods internally before required approval and ordering.
The scenario does not establish that a purchase order was issued.
No goods have been acknowledged as delivered.
An internal request does not establish invoice approval.

workshop.role_b: Supplier: order P44 shows twelve; can investigate the missing two and provide an update at three, but have no confirmed explanation yet.
workshop.challenge: The delivery note is signed. Keep the reported physical count separate from assumptions about what the signature proves.

modules.title: Welcoming visitors and checking arrangements
collocations: confirm the host: identify the employee expecting the visitor
check the appointment reference: match the visit to its recorded booking
issue the visitor badge: provide the appropriate pass after the required check
wait in reception: remain in the visitor area until the receiving arrangements are confirmed

case.brief: Visitor Taylor arrives for a 10:00 meeting with Jordan. The office has two Jordans: Jordan Chen in facilities and Jordan Patel in sales. Reference V12 names Jordan Chen. Check the reference, contact the host, and explain the reception wait; the visitor is not cleared to enter other areas alone.
case.model: We have two colleagues named Jordan, so could I check your appointment reference? V12 lists Jordan Chen in facilities. I'll contact that host now. Please wait here in reception while we confirm the receiving arrangements; I'll update you as soon as Jordan responds.

workshop.title: Check identity of the host without unnecessary questions
workshop.goal: Use the appointment reference to identify the right receiving colleague.
workshop.explanation: A shared first name is not enough to route a visitor. Ask for the relevant reference rather than private details unrelated to the visit.
frames: Could I check your appointment reference?
That lists ___ in ___.
Please wait here while I contact ___.
workshop.after: V12 names Jordan Chen in facilities; I'll contact that host before directing you further.
workshop.reason: The visitor gets a confirmed receiving person and a clear waiting location.

questions.prompt:
Visitor: I'm here for Jordan, reference V12.
Assistant: Your host is ____.
options: the colleague with the nearest desk
feedback: Correct. V12 identifies Jordan Chen in facilities.
That is the other Jordan, not the V12 host.
Availability does not change the named host for this visit.
Desk location does not identify the person responsible for V12.

questions.prompt:
Visitor: This pass shows my name, today's date, and the word Visitor. Is it for me or my car?
Assistant: It's your ____ for this visit.
feedback: Correct. The visitor badge identifies the guest under the visit arrangements.
An employee access card is not the guest's identification pass.
A parking permit concerns a vehicle, not the visitor's identification.
Delivery authorization concerns permission for goods, not this named visitor's identification.

workshop.role_b: Visitor: Taylor, booking V12, meeting Jordan at ten; do not know Jordan's surname.
workshop.challenge: The visitor sees someone wearing a badge and asks to follow them upstairs. Keep the host-confirmation arrangement clear.

modules.title: Clarifying travel options and booking status
collocations: check the fare conditions: read the rules attached to the quoted ticket
confirm the arrival station: verify the actual destination point
hold off on booking: wait before making a purchase or reservation
attach the supporting receipt: include the purchase record required for an expense request

case.brief: Two fictional rail quotes cover the same trip. A costs $70 and is nonrefundable; B costs $90 and permits a refund before departure with a $10 deduction. The traveler's meeting is not confirmed. Purchasing approval is still required. Compare the supplied conditions without recommending financial or legal action.
case.model: Both quotes cover the same trip. A costs seventy dollars and is nonrefundable; B costs ninety and allows a refund before departure with ten dollars deducted. Your meeting is still unconfirmed, so that flexibility may matter. Neither option is booked, and purchasing approval is still needed before we proceed.

workshop.title: Compare the actual conditions, not a broad label
workshop.goal: Explain price and cancellation flexibility using the supplied terms.
workshop.explanation: Refundable does not always mean every dollar comes back in every circumstance. Preserve the deadline and deduction attached to this fictional fare.
frames: Both cover ___, but their conditions differ.
Under these terms, cancellation before ___ means ___.
Neither is booked; we still need ___.
workshop.before: The ninety-dollar fare is fully refundable.
workshop.after: The ninety-dollar fare allows a refund before departure with a ten-dollar deduction.
workshop.reason: The wording preserves the actual limit rather than exaggerating flexibility.

questions.prompt:
Traveler: Would all ninety dollars come back if I cancel in time?
Assistant: No, the quoted fare is refundable ____.
feedback: Correct. That condition matches the supplied fare terms.
The quote explicitly includes a ten-dollar deduction.
The supplied refund condition applies before departure.
The terms do not promise refunds after missed departures.

questions.prompt:
Traveler: Have you bought either ticket?
Assistant: No, I have compared the quotes but ____.
feedback: Correct. Comparing quotes has not created a booking.
This says bookings were made, contrary to the case.
No payment confirmation is in progress here.
No purchase has been completed in the supplied facts.

workshop.role_b: Traveler: meeting might move; need a clear comparison and approval before any booking.
workshop.challenge: The traveler says refundable means no conditions. Read back the specific deduction and before-departure limit.

modules.title: Prioritizing work and handing over coverage
collocations: agree the priority order: decide which task should come first
flag a dependency: identify the missing input holding up a task
hand over an open item: transfer an unfinished task with its current status
confirm coverage: check who will handle named duties during an absence

case.brief: At 10:00 an assistant has a visitor list due at 10:30 and a room pack due at 11:00. Each needs thirty minutes. A manager requests a new twenty-minute spreadsheet check by 10:20. No colleague is free. Ask the manager to choose priorities or adjust a deadline; do not promise all three.
case.model: I have the visitor list due at ten-thirty and the room pack at eleven, each needing thirty minutes. The new check adds twenty minutes before ten-twenty, so I can't complete all three by those times. Which should take priority, and which deadline can we revise with the person waiting for it?

workshop.title: Make the conflict specific enough to resolve
workshop.goal: Negotiate task order using actual durations and agreed deadlines.
workshop.explanation: Describe the total workload and its timing, then ask the person with authority to choose. Don't quietly downgrade another person's deadline.
frames: I have ___ due at ___, requiring ___.
Adding ___ means ___ will be delayed.
Which deadline can we revise with ___?
workshop.before: I'll somehow fit it all in.
workshop.after: The added twenty-minute check conflicts with the existing deadlines; which task should move?
workshop.reason: The manager can make an informed choice rather than rely on an impossible promise.

questions.prompt:
Manager: At ten, do my twenty-minute check first, then the thirty-minute visitor list due at ten-thirty.
Assistant: That means ____.
options: the visitor list will miss its current deadline
the visitor list will still meet its current deadline
the room pack can start earlier than planned
the spreadsheet check will follow the visitor list
feedback: Correct. The check plus list need fifty minutes, beyond the ten-thirty deadline.
Only ten minutes would remain for the thirty-minute list after the check.
Adding work before the list delays rather than advances the room pack.
The manager explicitly asked for the spreadsheet check first.

questions.prompt:
Colleague: The room pack needs the final attendee list first.
Assistant: That list is a ____.
feedback: Correct. The pack depends on receiving that input.
A required input is not itself a completed transfer of responsibility.
The list is information, not a new completion time.
Coverage names who handles duties, not the input required here.

workshop.role_b: Manager: visitor list must stay at 10:30; can move the spreadsheet check to 11:20 while keeping the pack at eleven.
workshop.challenge: The manager calls the extra task urgent without changing its duration. Ask which existing commitment should change.

conversations.title: Whose three o'clock?
conversations.setting: An assistant checks a meeting request before sending invitations.
turns: Assistant
You asked for three o'clock. Which office's time zone did you mean for this meeting?
Colleague
Three here, please. I hadn't realized my message left that detail open for you.
Assistant
For this date, that's noon in their office. Both calendars show an opening then.
Colleague
Good. Could you reserve half an hour and include both local times in the invitation?
Assistant
Yes. Is this a confirmed meeting, or should I place a tentative hold while you ask Dana?
Colleague
A tentative hold. Dana still needs to agree, even though the calendar looks free.
Assistant
I'll mark it tentative and wait for your confirmation before describing it as accepted.
Colleague
Please allow fifteen minutes afterward as buffer time before my next call as well.
Assistant
The calendar permits that. I've held thirty minutes plus the separate fifteen-minute buffer.
Colleague
Thanks. I'll ask Dana today and tell you whether to confirm or release the hold.

conversations.title: Back-to-back meetings leave no travel time
conversations.setting: An assistant flags a scheduling conflict.
turns: Assistant
Your client meeting ends at two, and the next appointment starts across town at two.
Manager
I didn't notice the locations. That would leave no travel time between those appointments.
Assistant
The second host offered two-thirty as an alternative. Would you like me to check that slot?
Manager
Yes, but ask about the meeting length before moving anything already in the calendar.
Assistant
It's a thirty-minute discussion, and their two-thirty opening is still available this afternoon.
Manager
Then move the second appointment to two-thirty and keep the first one unchanged.
Assistant
I'll send the revised invitation and identify the location so nobody expects a video call.
Manager
Please ask the host to acknowledge the change rather than assume they saw the calendar update.
Assistant
They've accepted two-thirty at their office. Your first meeting still ends here at two.
Manager
Good. That leaves the agreed travel buffer, and I can prepare for the correct location.

conversations.title: One occurrence, not the whole series
conversations.setting: An assistant clarifies a recurring-meeting change.
turns: Assistant
You asked to move next Tuesday's team call. Should the later weekly meetings stay unchanged?
Colleague
Yes. Only next Tuesday needs moving because the visitor presentation overlaps with it.
Assistant
The recurring series is at ten. Do you want that one occurrence at eleven instead?
Colleague
Eleven works, and the usual thirty-minute length can stay the same for that date.
Assistant
I'll change the individual occurrence, not every future invitation in the series.
Colleague
Please make that clear in the update, because people may assume our weekly schedule has changed.
Assistant
The message will name the specific Tuesday date and confirm later weeks remain at ten.
Colleague
Can you also leave the original video link in place if the meeting system allows it?
Assistant
The updated invitation retains that link. I've checked the revised date and time before sending.
Colleague
I've received it. Only next Tuesday now shows eleven; the following week still shows ten.

additional_scenario.title: An all-day hold hides an available hour
additional_scenario.brief: A calendar shows an all-day tentative planning hold. The owner can release 1:00-2:00 for a supplier call but wants the rest kept. The supplier has not accepted.
additional_scenario.role_a: Assistant: clarify the partial release and keep supplier acceptance pending.
additional_scenario.role_b: Calendar owner: authorize only the one-hour release.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Can you clear that planning hold so I can speak to the supplier?
additional_scenario.complication: A colleague assumes the entire day is now free.
success_checks: Name the released hour.
Keep the rest of the hold intact.
Distinguish available time from supplier acceptance.

conversations.title: Delivery, not invoice payment
conversations.setting: An assistant routes a supplier's call.
turns: Assistant
Is your question about the invoice or the physical delivery, so I can reach the right team?
Caller
The delivery. I'm Lena Park, and our reference is D18. We need unloading arrangements.
Assistant
Facilities handles that at extension 214. Would you prefer a transfer or a callback request?
Caller
A callback, please. I need an answer before four if someone is available then.
Assistant
I'll include that requested time. I haven't confirmed the team's availability for a return call.
Caller
They have our office number from yesterday. Could you ask them to use that number again?
Assistant
I'll check the stored business contact rather than copy a number from a different supplier.
Caller
Please read the reference back as well; people sometimes hear B instead of D.
Assistant
D18, with D as in Delta, for facilities about unloading arrangements before four if possible.
Caller
That's correct. Please route it to facilities, not the accounts colleague I spoke to yesterday.

conversations.title: A similar surname needs spelling
conversations.setting: An assistant checks the intended recipient of a call.
turns: Assistant
Did you ask for Morgan Lee or Morgan Leigh? Both work in this building.
Caller
Morgan Leigh, ending G-H. We discussed next week's training room booking yesterday afternoon.
Assistant
Thank you. That Morgan is in learning support, on extension 306, rather than sales.
Caller
Yes, learning support is right. Could you put me through to that extension now?
Assistant
I can try. Would you like to leave a message if the extension isn't answered?
Caller
Yes. Please say the revised attendance count is eighteen, not the sixteen I gave yesterday.
Assistant
I'll pass on the changed count if needed. Is there a reference Morgan will recognize?
Caller
Training T52. You don't need the attendees' individual names for this particular message.
Assistant
Understood. Morgan Leigh, learning support, T52, revised count eighteen. I'll connect you now.
Caller
Thank you for checking the spelling; the wrong Morgan wouldn't know anything about the room.

conversations.title: A direct line is not a personal number
conversations.setting: An assistant responds to an external caller.
turns: Assistant
I can offer the team's published direct line or take a message for the colleague.
Caller
I was hoping for their personal mobile number so I could reach them this evening.
Assistant
I can't share a private number. The published direct line is the available business contact.
Caller
That's fine. Does calling the direct line guarantee they will answer rather than the team?
Assistant
No, it reaches their team contact point; I can't promise who will be available.
Caller
Then please take a message. I want to confirm the room booking reference A17.
Assistant
Certainly. I'll include A17 and your request for confirmation, without adding any private details.
Caller
Can you note that email is easier for me than another phone call today?
Assistant
Yes, I'll use the business email address already recorded for this booking and note that preference.
Caller
Thanks. A reply through that address will be enough; I don't need the personal number.

additional_scenario.title: A callback number was heard incorrectly
additional_scenario.brief: A caller gives a fictional number ending 0614, but the assistant repeats 0641. The caller needs a room-booking response before Friday; no callback time is agreed.
additional_scenario.role_a: Assistant: invite and acknowledge the correction.
additional_scenario.role_b: Caller: correct the final four digits and confirm the Friday need.
additional_scenario.opening_line: The last four digits are zero-six-one-four, not zero-six-four-one.
additional_scenario.complication: The caller interprets repeating Friday as a guaranteed callback deadline.
success_checks: Read back the corrected digits.
State the room-booking purpose.
Label Friday as requested rather than confirmed.

conversations.title: Quotes are an action, not an order
conversations.setting: An assistant helps close a short office meeting.
turns: Assistant
We have ten minutes left and two agenda items. Which should we finish today?
Chair
The printer decision needs attention first. Visitor signage can go on the next agenda.
Assistant
Sam offered to get two quotes by Thursday. Shall I confirm that as the action item?
Chair
Yes. Sam has accepted it, but we haven't approved buying a printer from either supplier.
Assistant
I'll record Sam as the owner and Thursday as the deadline for those two quotes.
Chair
Please don't call it a purchase decision in the minutes; we still need the comparison.
Assistant
Understood. Does the signage item need an interim action before the next meeting?
Chair
No. The current signs remain in place, and the review can wait until next Tuesday.
Assistant
Then the open purchase decision stays open, and signage is scheduled for Tuesday's agenda.
Chair
That's agreed. Please read those two points back to the attendees before we finish.

conversations.title: An action needs a person, not a department name
conversations.setting: An assistant checks a meeting note with a colleague.
turns: Assistant
My note says operations will check the room equipment. Who accepted that action during the meeting?
Colleague
I did. Please put my name, Mira, rather than leave it assigned to the whole department.
Assistant
What did you agree to check, and was there a deadline for reporting back?
Colleague
The screen connection and remote microphone, by Wednesday at noon, before Thursday's training session.
Assistant
I'll record both items and that deadline. Was fixing any fault also assigned to you?
Colleague
No. I'll report what works and raise any fault with support; I haven't promised repairs myself.
Assistant
Thanks. That gives the minutes a clear action without extending your responsibility beyond the discussion.
Colleague
Could you read the wording back? I want to make sure the deadline concerns my report.
Assistant
Mira checks the screen connection and microphone and reports the results by Wednesday noon.
Colleague
That matches. If there's a fault, the support request will be a separate follow-up.

conversations.title: A missing agenda attachment
conversations.setting: An assistant helps an attendee find the meeting information.
turns: Assistant
You received the calendar invitation, but said the agenda wasn't attached. Is the meeting time visible?
Attendee
Yes, Tuesday at ten is clear. I just don't know which topics need preparation.
Assistant
The agenda is in the shared meeting folder. I should have included the link.
Attendee
Could you send that link rather than another attachment that might become an older copy?
Assistant
Certainly. The current agenda has three items, and your presentation is the second one.
Attendee
How much time is allocated to it? I need to keep the example within the meeting limit.
Assistant
Ten minutes for the presentation and five for questions, according to the current agenda.
Attendee
That gives me fifteen in total. I'll plan the presentation for ten, not use all fifteen.
Assistant
I've sent the folder link. Please check that you can open it before the meeting.
Attendee
It opens now. I'll prepare ten minutes of presentation for the second agenda item.

additional_scenario.title: A meeting ends without a deadline
additional_scenario.brief: The team agrees that Leon will compare two room-booking systems, but no date is stated. Leon can provide a comparison Friday; the chair needs it Thursday and can accept an initial summary then.
additional_scenario.role_a: Assistant: invite a feasible deadline and distinguish summary from full comparison.
additional_scenario.role_b: Leon: offer Thursday's summary and Friday's full comparison.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Before we finish, when should Leon bring back the comparison?
additional_scenario.complication: An attendee assumes Thursday means the complete comparison.
success_checks: Name Leon as owner.
Confirm two distinct deliverables and dates.
Read back the agreed action aloud.

conversations.title: Correct guide, blocked link
conversations.setting: An assistant corrects an outdated visitor-guide attachment.
turns: Assistant
I sent version two earlier. Version three was approved this morning and corrects the reception floor.
Recipient
That explains the difference from the invitation. Which file should I use for tomorrow's visit?
Assistant
Version three in the shared folder. I'm sorry the earlier attachment gave the wrong floor.
Recipient
I've opened your new link, but I get an access-denied message rather than the guide.
Assistant
I'll ask the document owner to grant the viewing access you need for that file.
Recipient
Please don't make the whole folder public just for me; I only need the visitor guide.
Assistant
Agreed. I've requested access to that document. The owner has now confirmed the permission change.
Recipient
Let me try again. It opens, and version three says reception is on the second floor.
Assistant
That's the current information. Please use that link rather than the older downloaded attachment.
Recipient
I've marked the downloaded copy as old. I'll use this link tomorrow.

conversations.title: View access is enough for the task
conversations.setting: An assistant clarifies a colleague's file-access request.
turns: Assistant
You asked for access to the supplier schedule. Do you need to read it or update entries?
Colleague
Only read it. I'm checking the arrival times before I prepare the room list.
Assistant
Then viewing access is enough. I'll ask the document owner for it.
Colleague
I don't need edit rights, and I don't want to change anything accidentally while checking.
Assistant
Your access permission is view-only. The owner has sent the current file; can you open it?
Colleague
It opens now. I can see the Tuesday delivery but can't type in the cells.
Assistant
That's expected for viewing access. If you find an error, send it to the schedule owner.
Colleague
The room number on one line may be wrong. I'll ask the owner to confirm it.
Assistant
Please quote the delivery reference so they can find the exact entry you're questioning.
Colleague
I'll quote D43 and Tuesday's date when I ask the owner about that room.

conversations.title: An attachment name conceals an older revision
conversations.setting: An assistant checks two similarly named files with a colleague.
turns: Assistant
Both attachments are called final agenda, but their revision dates differ. Which one did the chair approve?
Colleague
The one revised at eleven today. The earlier file still has the old speaker order.
Assistant
I'll use the timestamp and the approved shared-folder copy, not the filename final by itself.
Colleague
Could you check that the opening speaker is Rosa before you send the agenda to attendees?
Assistant
The current approved copy lists Rosa first and Daniel second. That matches the chair's message.
Colleague
Good. Please send the link so people don't keep editing separate copies from their inboxes.
Assistant
I'll do that. What should I tell someone who already downloaded the earlier attachment?
Colleague
Ask them to use the current link; don't assume their downloaded copy updates automatically afterward.
Assistant
The message now names the eleven o'clock revision and explains that the speaker order changed.
Colleague
That's enough. Everyone can check the same current agenda before tomorrow's meeting starts.

additional_scenario.title: A link opens the template, not the completed document
additional_scenario.brief: A colleague sends a blank visitor-list template instead of the completed list for Thursday. The completed version is in a restricted shared folder. The requester already has viewing permission there.
additional_scenario.role_a: Assistant: identify the wrong file type and send the correct existing link.
additional_scenario.role_b: Requester: need Thursday's completed list, not a new template.
additional_scenario.opening_line: This opens a blank form; where are Thursday's attendees?
additional_scenario.complication: The sender assumes the requester wants to edit the template.
success_checks: Identify the completed Thursday list.
Keep the template separate.
Confirm the requester can view the corrected link without changing permissions.

conversations.title: Twelve on the note, ten in the shipment
conversations.setting: An assistant calls a supplier about archive boxes.
turns: Assistant
I'm calling about purchase order P44. We ordered twelve archive boxes, but the shipment contains ten.
Supplier
Our delivery note lists twelve. Have you checked whether two were packed in a separate package?
Assistant
We've checked the received shipment and have no second package or backorder notice recorded.
Supplier
Thank you. I'll ask dispatch to check the packing record for those two boxes.
Assistant
Could you confirm whether another package is due and tell us when you'll update us?
Supplier
I can give you an update at three today. I can't confirm another shipment yet.
Assistant
Three is helpful. We need the missing boxes for Friday, but haven't promised their arrival internally.
Supplier
I'll include that need in the query without changing the delivery date before dispatch responds.
Assistant
Please use P44 in your reply so we can keep it with the delivery note.
Supplier
I'll quote P44 when I call you at three with dispatch's update.

conversations.title: An internal request has not reached the supplier
conversations.setting: An assistant checks a colleague's supply request.
turns: Assistant
Your requisition for notebooks is in the internal approval queue. Have you received any purchasing confirmation?
Colleague
No. I assumed submitting the form meant the supplier had already been asked to deliver.
Assistant
Not yet. A purchase order hasn't been issued, so there isn't a confirmed supplier delivery date.
Colleague
We need them Monday. Could you ask the approver to review the request today?
Assistant
Yes. I'll add the Monday requirement and ask whether they can review it today.
Colleague
Please tell the team we're still waiting for approval, not expecting a confirmed Monday delivery.
Assistant
I will. I'll report the request status and any confirmed next step after the reviewer responds.
Colleague
Could we check the supply cupboard in the meantime for enough notebooks for the first session?
Assistant
There are six available. Would those cover the six attendees at Monday's opening session?
Colleague
Yes. Six cover Monday's group. Please keep the purchase request active for later sessions.

conversations.title: A backorder is not a new order
conversations.setting: An assistant discusses an undelivered part of an existing purchase.
turns: Assistant
Your message says the remaining four folders are on backorder. Are they still part of P58?
Supplier
Yes. Eight of the twelve were delivered; four remain outstanding under that same purchase order.
Assistant
Then I don't need to place a second order for four simply to keep the request active?
Supplier
Correct. A duplicate order could create another purchase. These four are still due on P58.
Assistant
Do you have a confirmed delivery date, or only an estimate at this stage?
Supplier
Only an estimate of next Thursday. We'll confirm once the shipment is actually arranged.
Assistant
Please label that as estimated in the update. Our team is deciding whether to use existing folders.
Supplier
I can do that. Would you also like notice if the estimate changes before dispatch?
Assistant
Please notify purchasing if the estimate changes, and copy our office inbox.
Supplier
Agreed. Four remain on backorder, with Thursday as an estimate. I'll contact purchasing.

additional_scenario.title: The right quantity but the wrong size
additional_scenario.brief: Order S31 specifies six A4 storage trays. Six letter-size trays arrived. Ordered A4 trays: TR-A4; delivered letter-size trays: TR-LTR. The supplier can review an exchange but no collection date is confirmed.
additional_scenario.role_a: Assistant: distinguish size mismatch from quantity shortage.
additional_scenario.role_b: Supplier: ask for the item codes and offer a review update tomorrow morning.
additional_scenario.opening_line: We received six trays, but their size differs from S31.
additional_scenario.complication: A colleague wants to reorder six before the supplier responds.
success_checks: Give the correct quantities and sizes.
Keep exchange review separate from confirmed replacement.
Avoid presenting a duplicate order as already required.

conversations.title: Two colleagues named Jordan
conversations.setting: An assistant identifies a visitor's host.
turns: Assistant
Welcome. You mentioned Jordan; could I check the appointment reference in your invitation first?
Visitor
It's V12, for ten o'clock. I don't remember whether Jordan works in facilities or sales.
Assistant
V12 lists Jordan Chen in facilities. We also have a Jordan Patel, so I'm glad we checked.
Visitor
Yes, the wrong Jordan wouldn't know why I brought these building plans with me.
Assistant
I'll contact Jordan Chen now. Please wait here in reception while we arrange for you to be met.
Visitor
Should I complete the visitor log now, or wait until Jordan confirms the meeting?
Assistant
Please sign the visitor log here while I contact your host about the room.
Visitor
There's Jordan on the phone. Can you ask whether the meeting is still in room four?
Assistant
Jordan confirms room four and will collect you from reception in a moment.
Visitor
Thank you. I'll wait by these chairs with my plans until Jordan arrives.

conversations.title: The visitor arrived at the old address
conversations.setting: An assistant helps a caller at a former office location.
turns: Assistant
You said the reception desk is closed. Which street address appears on the invitation you're using?
Visitor
Eighteen Harbor Street. I printed that invitation last month and came to the same entrance.
Assistant
Our current meeting invitation gives twenty-four Harbor Street. Did the update reach your email?
Visitor
I see the update now. I checked the time but missed the changed address.
Assistant
I'm sorry the address change wasn't clearer. I'll tell your host you're coming from number eighteen.
Visitor
I'm nearby but will be about ten minutes late. Could you tell the host before I walk over?
Assistant
Yes. The host confirms that arrival is workable and will wait at the current reception.
Visitor
Does the appointment reference remain V38, or did it change along with the address?
Assistant
It remains V38. Use twenty-four Harbor Street and the main reception entrance shown in the update.
Visitor
Twenty-four Harbor Street, V38. I'll be there in ten minutes.

conversations.title: A companion was not on the visitor list
conversations.setting: An assistant checks an additional visitor with the host.
turns: Assistant
The appointment lists one guest under V46, but two of you have arrived this morning.
Visitor
My colleague came with me to discuss the samples. I forgot to mention them to the host.
Assistant
I'll check with the host before arranging your colleague's access beyond reception.
Visitor
Can we both wait in reception while you check with the host?
Assistant
Certainly. May I tell the host your colleague's name and that they're joining the sample discussion?
Visitor
Yes, it's Robin Ellis. There are no changes to the samples or the meeting purpose.
Assistant
The host has confirmed Robin can join. We'll complete the separate visitor details for each of you.
Visitor
Thank you. Should Robin use my badge, or will there be a separate one issued?
Assistant
Robin needs a separate visitor badge after checking in; please keep your own.
Visitor
Understood. We'll complete our own details and wait here for the host to collect us.

additional_scenario.title: A visitor cannot stay for the delayed meeting
additional_scenario.brief: A 2:00 visitor can stay only until 2:30. The host is delayed until 2:20 and needs twenty minutes. The host can instead offer a video meeting tomorrow at nine.
additional_scenario.role_a: Assistant: relay the timing conflict and the host's alternative.
additional_scenario.role_b: Visitor: cannot stay past 2:30 but can attend tomorrow's video call.
additional_scenario.opening_line: If the meeting starts at twenty past, can we still finish by half past?
additional_scenario.complication: The visitor asks you to promise the host will cut the meeting in half.
success_checks: Calculate the ten-minute remaining window accurately.
Avoid shortening the host's meeting by assumption.
Confirm acceptance of tomorrow's alternative and requested invitation.

conversations.title: A cheaper fare with less flexibility
conversations.setting: An assistant compares two rail quotes with a traveler.
turns: Assistant
For this journey, it's seventy nonrefundable, or a ninety-dollar refundable fare with conditions.
Traveler
My meeting might move. What does conditional mean for the ninety-dollar fare you've found?
Assistant
The supplied terms allow a refund before departure with a ten-dollar deduction, not a full refund.
Traveler
That could matter. Does the seventy-dollar fare have the same cancellation option at a lower price?
Assistant
No, that quote is nonrefundable. I haven't booked either, and purchasing approval is still needed.
Traveler
Please send both options to the approver with those conditions, not just the headline prices.
Assistant
I will. Is the arrival station the same one listed on your meeting invitation?
Traveler
Yes, Central Station. I can reach the venue from there, but the meeting date remains unconfirmed.
Assistant
I'll hold the booking until both the meeting date and purchasing approval are confirmed.
Traveler
Thanks. Please contact me when the date and approval are settled, before buying anything.

conversations.title: A hotel date changed but the train did not
conversations.setting: An assistant checks a colleague's itinerary.
turns: Assistant
Your hotel starts Wednesday, but the itinerary still shows Tuesday's outbound train.
Traveler
The meeting moved a day. I changed the hotel, then forgot to ask about the train.
Assistant
Let's check the existing train booking reference and its conditions before discussing a change.
Traveler
The reference is T82. Please don't buy another ticket automatically while the original is still active.
Assistant
I won't. I'll ask the travel desk what changes are available under that booking.
Traveler
Could you keep the return date unchanged? The final session still ends on Friday afternoon.
Assistant
Yes. The request concerns the outbound date only, with Friday's return remaining as currently booked.
Traveler
The desk can review that today. Can you send me the revised itinerary only after confirmation?
Assistant
I'll mark Wednesday's outbound journey pending until the travel desk confirms the change.
Traveler
Good. I'll use the current reference for the query and wait before assuming the journey has moved.

conversations.title: A card statement is not the requested receipt
conversations.setting: An assistant explains missing support for an expense claim.
turns: Assistant
Your expense claim includes the card statement, but the travel policy asks for the itemized hotel receipt.
Traveler
I have a payment confirmation too. Does that show enough detail for this claim?
Assistant
It shows payment, but not the room nights and separate items requested in this policy.
Traveler
Then I need the hotel's itemized receipt. Can I ask them using my booking reference H39?
Assistant
Yes. Quote H39 and the stay dates so they can locate the relevant document.
Traveler
Please don't submit the claim as complete while I'm waiting for that missing receipt.
Assistant
I'll keep it marked incomplete and note which document remains outstanding for the reviewer.
Traveler
Could you check whether the train receipt is already included, so I don't request it again?
Assistant
It is attached and readable. The hotel receipt is the only missing item identified here.
Traveler
I'll ask the hotel for the receipt now and bring it back for checking.

additional_scenario.title: A conference venue has two nearby stations
additional_scenario.brief: The invitation names Riverside East station; an old itinerary names Riverside Central. Both are real destinations within this fictional exercise, and no ticket has been bought. The traveler needs the invitation's station.
additional_scenario.role_a: Assistant: identify the destination mismatch before requesting a quote.
additional_scenario.role_b: Traveler: confirm Riverside East and the conference date.
additional_scenario.opening_line: The station names are almost the same; does it matter which one is quoted?
additional_scenario.complication: A colleague says the cheaper quote must be correct.
success_checks: Confirm Riverside East by name.
Compare quotes for the same actual journey.
Keep price separate from destination correctness.

conversations.title: Three deadlines cannot all stay the same
conversations.setting: An assistant negotiates competing tasks with a manager.
turns: Assistant
Both original tasks take thirty minutes: visitor list by ten-thirty, room pack by eleven.
Manager
Please do a twenty-minute spreadsheet check first, by ten-twenty. Can the other tasks still fit?
Assistant
Not without delaying an existing deadline. No colleague is free; which commitment can we move?
Manager
The visitor list must stay at ten-thirty. Could the room pack be finished a little later instead?
Assistant
The training starts at eleven, so the trainer would need to agree to that delay.
Manager
Keep both original deadlines. I'll accept the spreadsheet check at eleven-twenty, after the pack.
Assistant
That gives each task the stated time. I'll tell you if a missing input changes the schedule.
Manager
Please do. The spreadsheet can wait, but the visitor list must reach reception on time.
Assistant
Visitor list first, room pack second, and your spreadsheet check by eleven-twenty.
Manager
Agreed. I'll tell the person waiting for the check that I've accepted the revised time.

conversations.title: Coverage includes the phone, not every pending task
conversations.setting: An assistant arranges lunch coverage.
turns: Assistant
Could you cover the reception phone from twelve to twelve-thirty while I take lunch?
Colleague
Yes. Am I also taking over the supplier follow-up due at one, or only the phone?
Assistant
Only the phone. I'll return before the one o'clock follow-up and keep responsibility for it.
Colleague
Then please show me where the call-routing list is and which colleague handles urgent delivery questions.
Assistant
The list is beside the phone. Facilities extension 214 handles delivery arrangements during that period.
Colleague
I'll take messages and use that route if a delivery caller needs the team.
Assistant
Thank you. There's a visitor expected at twelve-fifteen; their host knows to meet them here.
Colleague
I can greet them and contact the host, but I won't change their room booking independently.
Assistant
That's enough coverage. I'll be back at twelve-thirty and check any messages with you.
Colleague
Fine. I'll keep the messages in the normal record and give you a short handover.

conversations.title: The missing list is holding up the room pack
conversations.setting: An assistant gives a status update to a trainer.
turns: Assistant
The room pack is ready except for the final attendee list, which hasn't reached us yet.
Trainer
I sent a draft yesterday with fourteen names. Can't you use that as the final list?
Assistant
Yesterday's draft left two places unconfirmed. Has their attendance changed since then?
Trainer
Those two have now accepted. I'll send the confirmed list of sixteen this morning.
Assistant
Thank you. What time can you send it so I can prepare the correct number of packs?
Trainer
By ten-fifteen. The session starts at eleven, and I need the packs delivered by ten-forty-five.
Assistant
That works if the confirmed list arrives then. I'll prepare the unchanged materials while I wait.
Trainer
Please avoid printing names from the draft if any corrections appear on the final version.
Assistant
I will. The final list is the dependency; the other material can be prepared now.
Trainer
I'll send the confirmed sixteen names by ten-fifteen and highlight the changed entries.

additional_scenario.title: A handover recipient is unavailable
additional_scenario.brief: The usual afternoon cover is absent. A callback to supplier D55 is due at four. The supervisor can assign Jamie, who is available from three. No reassignment has been confirmed.
additional_scenario.role_a: Assistant: ask the supervisor to confirm a named replacement.
additional_scenario.role_b: Supervisor: can assign Jamie and request explicit acceptance.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Who will take the four o'clock supplier callback now that our usual cover is absent?
additional_scenario.complication: A note saying 'afternoon team' is treated as enough.
success_checks: Name D55 and the callback time.
Ask for a specific owner rather than a broad group.
Confirm Jamie's acceptance before treating coverage as settled.

dialogues.title: A daylight-saving assumption needs a date check
dialogues.setting: An assistant and colleague review a cross-office invitation using a supplied date-specific conversion.
dialogue: Assistant
The draft uses last month's time difference. Our verified conversion for this meeting date is different.
Colleague
I copied the old invitation. What local times should appear for the new date?
Assistant
The calendar shows nine here and three there, not the four shown in the draft.
Colleague
Then the other office may have reserved the wrong hour. Please check before confirming the meeting.
Assistant
I'll contact their administrator with the date and both proposed local times. Our nine remains a hold.
Colleague
Could you ask whether their room is available at three too, rather than check only the person's calendar?
Assistant
I've asked. The participant can attend at three, but their room is occupied until three-thirty.
Colleague
We can meet by video without that room. Does the participant have another suitable place available?
Assistant
They confirm a smaller room at three. I'll update the invitation with the corrected local times.
Colleague
Please state that the earlier four o'clock reference was an error, so nobody relies on it.
Assistant
Done. Both participants have accepted the corrected invitation, and the old time is identified in the correction.
Colleague
Thanks. I'll use this meeting's date-specific times rather than carry the old difference into future bookings.
notes: 'For this meeting date' limits a time conversion to the date verified.
'Remains a hold' keeps scheduling progress distinct from final acceptance.

dialogues.title: A message for an absent colleague
dialogues.setting: An assistant helps a caller reach the right backup contact.
dialogue: Assistant
Alex is away today. Would you like to leave a message or speak with the covering coordinator?
Caller
I need to change tomorrow's delivery window. Leaving it until Alex returns would be too late.
Assistant
The covering coordinator handles delivery changes. Could I confirm the reference before connecting your call?
Caller
It's D27, and the driver now expects to arrive at two instead of the agreed morning slot.
Assistant
I'll pass on the requested change, not describe two as accepted before the coordinator checks it.
Caller
Good. We can keep the original arrangement if the afternoon isn't possible, but need an answer today.
Assistant
That fallback is useful. May I tell the coordinator both the proposed time and the original alternative?
Caller
Yes. Please also say the delivery size hasn't changed; it's only the proposed arrival time.
Assistant
I've briefed them. They can take your call now and discuss whether the new window is possible.
Caller
Will I have to repeat my business number, or can you transfer the call directly to their extension?
Assistant
I can transfer you directly. If we disconnect, use the published direct line and quote D27.
Caller
Thank you. Please put me through; I can confirm the final window with the person arranging access.
notes: 'Requested change' prevents a caller's proposal from being mistaken for an accepted schedule.
'The covering coordinator' identifies the available person taking an absent colleague's duties.

dialogues.title: An absent attendee is not automatically an action owner
dialogues.setting: An assistant checks whether a proposed task was accepted.
dialogue: Assistant
The draft minutes assign the visitor guide to Noor, but Noor wasn't at today's meeting.
Chair
Someone suggested Noor would be suitable. We didn't actually ask whether they could take it on.
Assistant
Then I'll record that as a proposed owner rather than an accepted assignment in the minutes.
Chair
Please ask Noor now; we need a first outline by Friday to discuss on Monday.
Assistant
I've spoken to Noor. They can review an outline Friday, but can't prepare it from scratch this week.
Chair
That changes the task. I can prepare the first outline Thursday and ask Noor to review it.
Assistant
Shall I record you as the drafting owner and Noor as reviewer, with those separate dates?
Chair
Yes. Please confirm Noor accepts the review before treating the revised arrangement as agreed.
Assistant
Noor has accepted Friday's review. They ask for the Thursday draft by four so they can plan their time.
Chair
I can send it by four. Monday's meeting can discuss the reviewed outline, not a finished published guide.
Assistant
I'll read back the sequence: your draft Thursday, Noor's review Friday, and discussion on Monday.
Chair
That's correct. The minutes now reflect what each person actually accepted rather than the first suggestion.
notes: 'Proposed owner' distinguishes a suggestion from accepted responsibility.
'Drafting owner' and 'reviewer' separate two different tasks on the same document.

dialogues.title: A correction after the document has been printed
dialogues.setting: An assistant coordinates an update to already printed meeting packs.
dialogue: Assistant
Version four corrects the room, but you printed version three. How many packs are ready?
Colleague
Twelve. The meeting content is unchanged, but the front page sends people to room 210 instead of 201.
Assistant
The owner confirmed room 201. The printed packs need correcting too, not just the shared file.
Colleague
Could I replace just the front page rather than reprint the eleven unchanged pages in every pack?
Assistant
The owner has approved replacing that page. Please keep the revision label visible so the corrected packs are identifiable.
Colleague
I'll replace the fronts and check each pack. Are any already with attendees outside this room?
Assistant
Two were collected earlier by visitors. I'll contact their host and explain the corrected room number directly.
Colleague
Please ask for acknowledgment, since a new file in the folder won't change their printed copies.
Assistant
The host has confirmed both visitors know room 201 and will receive the corrected front page on arrival.
Colleague
I've finished the ten remaining packs here. All now show room 201 and the version-four label.
Assistant
The folder is current, these ten packs are corrected, and the host is handling the other two.
Colleague
I'll put a corrected pack by the entrance for the chair when they arrive.
notes: 'As well as the link' identifies a correction needed in another medium.
'Already with attendees' checks who may still rely on a superseded printed copy.

dialogues.title: The supplier offers a substitute color
dialogues.setting: An assistant coordinates a choice without changing a colleague's request silently.
dialogue: Assistant
The requisition specified black desk organizers, and P63 carries that description. Your message offers gray instead.
Supplier
Black is on backorder. We can supply six gray organizers tomorrow if you accept the substitution today.
Assistant
The requesting team chose black to match existing storage. I need their decision before changing the order.
Supplier
Understood. The quoted unit price would stay the same, but the color would differ from your purchase order.
Assistant
Please hold the proposal while I check. Does waiting for black have a confirmed delivery date yet?
Supplier
No confirmed date. We expect an update Friday, but that isn't a promise that black stock arrives then.
Assistant
I've reached the requester. They can accept gray for all six if the stated price remains unchanged.
Supplier
The price remains as quoted. Please have your purchasing contact confirm the revised item description through your normal process.
Assistant
I'll ask purchasing to confirm the accepted color change; I haven't changed the order myself.
Supplier
That's fine. We'll keep the substitution pending until the purchasing confirmation reaches us, then confirm delivery arrangements.
Assistant
The team knows gray is accepted internally, but we're waiting for revised supplier confirmation.
Supplier
I'll acknowledge the purchasing confirmation when received, then send the actual delivery arrangements.
notes: 'Hold the proposal' pauses a decision without cancelling the existing order.
'Accepted internally' distinguishes a team's preference from supplier order confirmation.

dialogues.title: An early visitor needs somewhere to wait
dialogues.setting: An assistant checks arrangements for a visitor who arrives well before their appointment.
dialogue: Assistant
Your appointment is at two. It's twelve-thirty now; did the host ask you to arrive early?
Visitor
No, my train was earlier than expected. Could I work in your meeting room until the host is available?
Assistant
That room is booked until one-forty-five. I can ask about a waiting space, but can't offer it now.
Visitor
I don't need the meeting room specifically. Somewhere to sit with my own laptop would be enough.
Assistant
There is a visitor seating area here in reception. The host confirms you may wait there until collected.
Visitor
That works. Can I leave my bag with you while I get a drink from the cafe?
Assistant
We don't provide unattended bag storage here. You can keep it with you or use another arrangement yourself.
Visitor
I'll keep it with me. Could you tell the host I've arrived without asking them to leave their current meeting?
Assistant
I've sent your arrival message. The two o'clock appointment remains unchanged.
Visitor
Thank you. I'm not asking for an earlier meeting, just avoiding another trip back from the station.
Assistant
The host will meet you here at two. Please wait in this reception area.
Visitor
I'll sit here with my bag and laptop until two. Thanks for checking.
notes: 'Not asking for an earlier meeting' separates arrival from a requested schedule change.
'Can't offer it now' ties a limit to a concrete room booking.

dialogues.title: A reservation request without a confirmation number
dialogues.setting: An assistant checks whether a hotel room is actually reserved.
dialogue: Assistant
The hotel email says request received, but contains no confirmed reservation or booking reference.
Traveler
I thought that meant my room was booked. I need to know before arranging the journey.
Assistant
I'll contact the travel desk. Your itinerary should show the hotel request as pending until they confirm it.
Traveler
Please ask about the Tuesday arrival and two-night stay; the dates changed in an earlier message.
Assistant
They've confirmed the requested dates were correct, but the first hotel hasn't accepted the reservation.
Traveler
Is there another quoted option, or do we need to wait without a room for that trip?
Assistant
A second hotel has availability at the approved rate. The travel desk needs your preference before requesting it.
Traveler
The second location works. Please proceed through the existing approval arrangement and ask for the confirmation.
Assistant
The desk has now supplied booking reference H74 for Tuesday arrival and two nights at the second hotel.
Traveler
Can you remove the first hotel's name from the confirmed section of my itinerary so I don't go there?
Assistant
The itinerary now shows the second hotel and H74; the first request is closed without confirmation.
Traveler
I've checked it. I'll use that address and reference, and keep the confirmation with the itinerary.
notes: 'Request received' is weaker than a confirmed reservation.
'Confirmed section' makes the status of an itinerary entry explicit.

dialogues.title: Friday coverage with one unanswered supplier query
dialogues.setting: An assistant hands open work to the colleague providing afternoon coverage.
dialogue: Assistant
Your two-to-five coverage includes one open supplier query under purchase order P77.
Covering colleague
What is confirmed, and what response are we waiting for before I contact the supplier this afternoon?
Assistant
Six chairs arrived, but one has a different code. The supplier is checking whether it was a substitution.
Covering colleague
Has anyone agreed to keep the different chair, or should I avoid describing it as accepted?
Assistant
Nobody has accepted it. The requesting team wants the ordered model, and the supplier promised an update at four.
Covering colleague
I'll follow up at four if no update arrives. Where can I find the item codes and delivery note?
Assistant
They're linked in the shift handover folder under P77. The photograph shows the labels, without any personal information.
Covering colleague
I can open both. If they offer a replacement date, who needs to confirm whether it suits us?
Assistant
Facilities must confirm the date against their receiving schedule; please ask their coordinator.
Covering colleague
I'll do that. My coverage includes the four o'clock query and passing any proposed date to facilities.
Assistant
Please record the supplier's actual response, even if the mismatch remains unresolved at four.
Covering colleague
Accepted. I'll report the status before five and keep the different model separate from any agreed replacement.
notes: 'Nobody has accepted it' prevents receipt from being mistaken for agreement to a substitution.
'My coverage includes' confirms the exact task taken over for a limited period.
